audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel / Shemuel Bet chapter 1, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for the messenger's conflicting Saul-death account, Amalekite identity, crown and bracelet, mourning, summary execution, the Bow lament, Jonathan-David love language, women mourners, Gilboa curse, and weapon-fall refrain.

verses.restored: After death of Saul, David returned from striking Amalek and stayed two days in Ziklag.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;

modern.text: After the death of Saul, David returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites and stayed in Ziklag two days.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַֽחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת שָׁא֔וּל וְדָוִ֣ד שָׁ֔ב מֵהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת הָעֲמָלֵ֑ק וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב דָּוִ֛ד בְּצִקְלָ֖ג יָמִ֥ים שְׁנָֽיִם

verses.restored: On third day, look, a man came from camp, from with Saul, with garments torn and earth upon his head. When he came to David, he fell to ground and bowed.

familiar.text: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.

modern.text: On the third day a man with torn clothes and dust on his head arrived from Saul’s camp. When he came to David, he fell to the ground to pay him homage.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י וְהִנֵּה֩ אִ֨ישׁ בָּ֤א מִן הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ מֵעִ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל וּבְגָדָ֣יו קְרֻעִ֔ים וַאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיְהִי֙ בְּבֹא֣וֹ אֶל דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּפֹּ֥ל אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ

verses.restored: David said to him, From where have you come? He said to him, From camp of Israel I escaped.

familiar.text: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.

modern.text: “Where have you come from?” David asked. “I have escaped from the Israelite camp,” he replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה תָּב֑וֹא וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו מִמַּחֲנֵ֥ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נִמְלָֽטְתִּי

verses.restored: David said to him, What was matter? Please tell me. He said, People fled from battle, and also many of people fell and died; Saul and Jonathan his son also died.

familiar.text: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.

modern.text: “What was the outcome?” David asked. “Please tell me.” “The troops fled from the battle,” he replied. “Many of them fell and died. And Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֥יו דָּוִ֛ד מֶה הָיָ֥ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַגֶּד נָ֣א לִ֑י וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֲשֶׁר נָ֨ס הָעָ֜ם מִן הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְגַם הַרְבֵּ֞ה נָפַ֤ל מִן הָעָם֙ וַיָּמֻ֔תוּ וְגַ֗ם שָׁא֛וּל וִיהוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ מֵֽתוּ

verses.restored: David said to young man who told him, How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son died?

familiar.text: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?

modern.text: Then David asked the young man who had brought him the report, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד אֶל הַנַּ֖עַר הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֑וֹ אֵ֣יךְ יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּי מֵ֥ת שָׁא֖וּל וִיהֽוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנֽוֹ

verses.restored: Young man who told him said, By chance I was on mount Gilboa, and look, Saul was leaning upon his spear, and look, chariots and horsemen pressed close to him.

familiar.text: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.

modern.text: “I happened to be on Mount Gilboa,” he replied, “and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and the cavalry closing in on him.

original.text: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר הַנַּ֣עַר הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֗וֹ נִקְרֹ֤א נִקְרֵ֨יתִי֙ בְּהַ֣ר הַגִּלְבֹּ֔עַ וְהִנֵּ֥ה שָׁא֖וּל נִשְׁעָ֣ן עַל חֲנִית֑וֹ וְהִנֵּ֥ה הָרֶ֛כֶב וּבַעֲלֵ֥י הַפָּרָשִׁ֖ים הִדְבִּקֻֽהוּ

verses.restored: He turned behind him, saw me, and called to me. I said, Look, I am here.

familiar.text: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I.

modern.text: When he turned around and saw me, he called out and I answered, ‘Here I am!’

original.text: וַיִּ֥פֶן אַחֲרָ֖יו וַיִּרְאֵ֑נִי וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֵלָ֔י וָאֹמַ֖ר הִנֵּֽנִי

verses.restored: He said to me, Who are you? I said to him, I am an Amalekite.

familiar.text: And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.

modern.text: ‘Who are you?’ he asked. So I told him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֖י מִי אָ֑תָּה ויאמר אֵלָ֔יו עֲמָלֵקִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי

verses.restored: He said to me, Please stand over me and put me to death, because agony has seized me, though all my life is still in me.

familiar.text: He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me.

modern.text: Then he begged me, ‘Stand over me and kill me, for agony has seized me, but my life still lingers.’

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י עֲמָד נָ֤א עָלַי֙ וּמֹ֣תְתֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י אֲחָזַ֖נִי הַשָּׁבָ֑ץ כִּֽי כָל ע֥וֹד נַפְשִׁ֖י בִּֽי

verses.restored: I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew he could not live after his fall. I took crown that was upon his head and bracelet that was upon his arm, and I brought them here to my lord.

familiar.text: So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.

modern.text: So I stood over him and killed him, because I knew that after he had fallen he could not survive. And I took the crown that was on his head and the band that was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”

original.text: וָאֶעֱמֹ֤ד עָלָיו֙ וַאֲמֹ֣תְתֵ֔הוּ כִּ֣י יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י לֹ֥א יִֽחְיֶ֖ה אַחֲרֵ֣י נִפְל֑וֹ וָאֶקַּ֞ח הַנֵּ֣זֶר אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל רֹאשׁ֗וֹ וְאֶצְעָדָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל זְרֹע֔וֹ וָאֲבִיאֵ֥ם אֶל אֲדֹנִ֖י הֵֽנָּה

verses.restored: David took hold of his garments and tore them, and so did all men who were with him.

familiar.text: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him:

modern.text: Then David took hold of his own clothes and tore them, and all the men who were with him did the same.

original.text: וַיַּחֲזֵ֥ק דָּוִ֛ד בבגדו וַיִּקְרָעֵ֑ם וְגַ֥ם כָּל הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: They mourned, wept, and fasted until evening for Saul, for Jonathan his son, for people of YHWH, and for house of Israel, because they had fallen by sword.

familiar.text: And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.

modern.text: They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

original.text: וַֽיִּסְפְּדוּ֙ וַיִּבְכּ֔וּ וַיָּצֻ֖מוּ עַד הָעָ֑רֶב עַל שָׁא֞וּל וְעַל יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בְּנ֗וֹ וְעַל עַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ וְעַל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י נָפְל֖וּ בֶּחָֽרֶב

verses.restored: David said to young man who told him, From where are you? He said, I am son of a resident alien, an Amalekite.

familiar.text: And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.

modern.text: And David inquired of the young man who had brought him the report, “Where are you from?” “I am the son of a foreigner,” he answered. “I am an Amalekite.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶל הַנַּ֨עַר֙ הַמַּגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה אָ֑תָּה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בֶּן אִ֛ישׁ גֵּ֥ר עֲמָלֵקִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי

verses.restored: David said to him, How were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy anointed of YHWH?

familiar.text: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?

modern.text: So David asked him, “Why were you not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD’s anointed?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלָ֖יו דָּוִ֑ד אֵ֚יךְ לֹ֣א יָרֵ֔אתָ לִשְׁלֹ֨חַ֙ יָֽדְךָ֔ לְשַׁחֵ֖ת אֶת מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: David called one of young men and said, Approach; strike him. He struck him, and he died.

familiar.text: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.

modern.text: Then David summoned one of the young men and said, “Go, execute him!” So the young man struck him down, and he died.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א דָוִ֗ד לְאַחַד֙ מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֔ים וַיֹּ֖אמֶר גַּ֣שׁ פְּגַע בּ֑וֹ וַיַּכֵּ֖הוּ וַיָּמֹֽת

verses.restored: David said to him, Your blood is upon your head, because your mouth testified against you, saying, I put anointed of YHWH to death.

familiar.text: And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the LORD’s anointed.

modern.text: For David had said to the Amalekite, “Your blood be on your own head because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I killed the LORD’s anointed.’” David’s Song for Saul and Jonathan

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ דָּוִ֔ד דמיך עַל רֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּ֣י פִ֗יךָ עָנָ֤ה בְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָנֹכִ֥י מֹתַ֖תִּי אֶת מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: David lamented with this lament over Saul and over Jonathan his son.

familiar.text: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:

modern.text: Then David took up this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,

original.text: וַיְקֹנֵ֣ן דָּוִ֔ד אֶת הַקִּינָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את עַל שָׁא֖וּל וְעַל יְהוֹנָתָ֥ן בְּנֽוֹ

verses.restored: He said to teach children of Judah the Bow. Look, it is written in Book of Jashar/Upright.

familiar.text: (Also he bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jasher.)

modern.text: and he ordered that the sons of Judah be taught the Song of the Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לְלַמֵּ֥ד בְּנֵֽי יְהוּדָ֖ה קָ֑שֶׁת הִנֵּ֥ה כְתוּבָ֖ה עַל סֵ֥פֶר הַיָּשָֽׁר

verses.restored: Beauty/glory of Israel is slain upon your high places. How have mighty fallen!

familiar.text: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!

modern.text: “Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!

original.text: הַצְּבִי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַל בָּמוֹתֶ֖יךָ חָלָ֑ל אֵ֖יךְ נָפְל֥וּ גִבּוֹרִֽים

verses.restored: Do not tell it in Gath; do not announce it in streets of Ashkelon, lest daughters of Philistines rejoice, lest daughters of uncircumcised exult.

familiar.text: Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

modern.text: Tell it not in Gath; proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised exult.

original.text: אַל תַּגִּ֣ידוּ בְגַ֔ת אַֽל תְּבַשְּׂר֖וּ בְּחוּצֹ֣ת אַשְׁקְל֑וֹן פֶּן תִּשְׂמַ֨חְנָה֙ בְּנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים פֶּֽן תַּעֲלֹ֖זְנָה בְּנ֥וֹת הָעֲרֵלִֽים

verses.restored: Mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew and no rain upon you, nor fields of offerings, because there shield of mighty was defiled, shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.

familiar.text: Ye mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew, neither let there be rain, upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, as though he had not been anointed with oil.

modern.text: O mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, no fields yielding offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.

original.text: הָרֵ֣י בַגִּלְבֹּ֗עַ אַל טַ֧ל וְאַל מָטָ֛ר עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם וּשְׂדֵ֣י תְרוּמֹ֑ת כִּ֣י שָׁ֤ם נִגְעַל֙ מָגֵ֣ן גִּבּוֹרִ֔ים מָגֵ֣ן שָׁא֔וּל בְּלִ֖י מָשִׁ֥יחַ בַּשָּֽׁמֶן

verses.restored: From blood of slain, from fat of mighty, bow of Jonathan did not turn back, and sword of Saul did not return empty.

familiar.text: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.

modern.text: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not retreat, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.

original.text: מִדַּ֣ם חֲלָלִ֗ים מֵחֵ֨לֶב֙ גִּבּוֹרִ֔ים קֶ֚שֶׁת יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן לֹ֥א נָשׂ֖וֹג אָח֑וֹר וְחֶ֣רֶב שָׁא֔וּל לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב רֵיקָֽם

verses.restored: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided; swifter than eagles, stronger than lions.

familiar.text: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

modern.text: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in life, were not divided in death. They were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

original.text: שָׁא֣וּל וִיהוֹנָתָ֗ן הַנֶּאֱהָבִ֤ים וְהַנְּעִימִם֙ בְּחַיֵּיהֶ֔ם וּבְמוֹתָ֖ם לֹ֣א נִפְרָ֑דוּ מִנְּשָׁרִ֣ים קַ֔לּוּ מֵאֲרָי֖וֹת גָּבֵֽרוּ

verses.restored: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with delights, who placed ornaments of gold upon your clothing.

familiar.text: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with other delights, who put on ornaments of gold upon your apparel.

modern.text: O daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and luxury, who decked your garments with ornaments of gold.

original.text: בְּנוֹת֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל שָׁא֖וּל בְּכֶ֑ינָה הַמַּלְבִּֽשְׁכֶ֤ם שָׁנִי֙ עִם עֲדָנִ֔ים הַֽמַּעֲלֶה֙ עֲדִ֣י זָהָ֔ב עַ֖ל לְבוּשְׁכֶֽן

verses.restored: How have mighty fallen in midst of battle! Jonathan is slain upon your high places.

familiar.text: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, thou wast slain in thine high places.

modern.text: How the mighty have fallen in the thick of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.

original.text: אֵ֚יךְ נָפְל֣וּ גִבֹּרִ֔ים בְּת֖וֹךְ הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן עַל בָּמוֹתֶ֖יךָ חָלָֽל

verses.restored: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan. Very pleasant you were to me. Wonderful was your love to me, surpassing love of women.

familiar.text: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.

modern.text: I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were delightful to me; your love to me was extraordinary, surpassing the love of women.

original.text: צַר לִ֣י עָלֶ֗יךָ אָחִי֙ יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן נָעַ֥מְתָּ לִּ֖י מְאֹ֑ד נִפְלְאַ֤תָה אַהֲבָֽתְךָ֙ לִ֔י מֵאַהֲבַ֖ת נָשִֽׁים

verses.restored: How have mighty fallen, and weapons of war perished!

familiar.text: How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!

modern.text: How the mighty have fallen and the weapons of war have perished!”

original.text: אֵ֚יךְ נָפְל֣וּ גִבּוֹרִ֔ים וַיֹּאבְד֖וּ כְּלֵ֥י מִלְחָמָֽה

translation_notes: The messenger's claim that he killed Saul conflicts with 1 Samuel 31, where Saul falls on his own sword. The narrative may portray a true report, a mercy-killing claim, opportunistic fabrication, or a separate tradition; the tension must remain visible.
The messenger is both Amalekite and son of a resident alien. His ethnicity does not explain guilt and must not support inherited enmity, xenophobia, or modern Amalek labeling.
David orders immediate execution based on the man's own testimony. The text provides no trial, witnesses, or opportunity for defense; this is summary royal violence, not a due-process model.
Saul's alleged request to be killed occurs under catastrophic battlefield injury. It may not become instruction for assisted death, suicide, or killing a distressed person.
David's lament honors Saul without erasing Saul's violence against David, Michal, Jonathan, priests, and civilians. Grief does not require historical absolution.
Jonathan's love is described as wonderful and surpassing the love of women. Queer readings may not be erased, while no single modern identity label should be forced upon the ancient relationship.
The lament's contemptuous circumcision language and silencing of Philistine women belong to ancient wartime rhetoric and may not authorize genital shame, misogyny, or ethnic hatred.
The final refrain calls warriors and weapons fallen; it is lament, not war recruitment.
